title: Historical V54 - Docker Setup
summary: The preferred Docker setup guide for building and running SMTO all-services, then wiring required gateways and an OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint.

headings.title: Or Host vLLM Locally With Conda

html:
Historical reference. See the current V55 architecture guide before using this material.

Docker Setup

This is the preferred product setup after cloning or syncing the source. The all-services Docker stack builds SMTO from the repository and runs the Agent runtime, Agent UI, manual, website, and audio runtime. Gateways and LLM servers remain outside the stack because they belong on the machines that own shell execution, terminals, GPUs, model weights, and private workspaces.

The correct high-level order is:

  1. Build the all-services Docker image.
  2. Start the all-services compose stack.
  3. Install and start one or more native gateways.
  4. Attach an existing OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint or start local vLLM.
  5. Validate service, gateway, and model health.
  6. Open the Agent UI and run a read-only request.

Docker Architecture

The preferred stack uses:

  • docker/server.Dockerfile to build the shared image;
  • docker-all-services/docker-compose.yaml to run the product stack;
  • docker-all-services/build.sh to build the image;
  • docker-all-services/start.sh to start the stack;
  • a named Docker volume, smto-all-services-data, mounted at /data.
Service Container name Purpose Host port
server smto-all-server Agent runtime and Agent UI 8011
audio smto-all-audio Audio transcription runtime internal 8012
manual smto-all-manual Searchable manual 8013
website smto-all-website Product website 8014

The server container is configured with:

AOR_GATEWAY_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8787
AOR_AVAILABLE_NODES=localhost
AOR_DEFAULT_NODE=localhost
AOR_AUDIO_TRANSCRIBER_SERVICE_URL=http://audio:8012

The LLM endpoint defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 unless changed in the Agent UI settings or by an explicit bootstrap config.

flowchart LR subgraph Docker["docker-all-services"] Server[server\nAgent UI + API\n8011] Audio[audio\ntranscription\n8012 internal] Manual[manual\n8013] Website[website\n8014] Data[(smto-all-services-data\n/data)] Server --> Audio Server --> Data Audio --> Data Manual --> Data Website --> Server Website --> Manual end Server --> Gateway[Native gateway\nhost.docker.internal:8787] Server --> LLM[OpenAI-compatible LLM\n/v1]

Requirements

Use a machine with:

  • Git and a synced SMTO source tree.
  • Docker Engine with Compose v2.
  • Enough disk space for the image, Python dependencies, Playwright Chromium, audio assets, local databases, and generated artifacts.
  • curl for validation checks.
  • Python 3.11 or newer on every gateway machine.
  • Conda or Miniconda if you plan to create a local vllm environment.
  • A reachable OpenAI-compatible model endpoint, or GPU hardware suitable for the vLLM model profile you choose.

Build The All-Services Image

From the repository root:

./docker-all-services/build.sh

Build a tagged version:

./docker-all-services/build.sh v1.0.0

The script builds from docker/server.Dockerfile and uses these defaults:

SMTO_IMAGE=smto-all-services
SMTO_VERSION=latest

It also passes AOR_BUILD_AUDIO=1, so this is the Docker path that builds the local whisper-cli binary for voice dictation.

Start The All-Services Stack

Start in the foreground:

./docker-all-services/start.sh

Start in the background:

./docker-all-services/start.sh -d

Start a tagged version:

./docker-all-services/start.sh v1.0.0

Open:

Page URL
Agent UI http://127.0.0.1:8011/agent-ui
Runtime health http://127.0.0.1:8011/healthz
Manual http://127.0.0.1:8013/manual
Manual health http://127.0.0.1:8013/healthz
Website http://127.0.0.1:8014/website
Website health http://127.0.0.1:8014/healthz

View logs:

docker compose -f docker-all-services/docker-compose.yaml logs -f
docker compose -f docker-all-services/docker-compose.yaml logs -f server
docker compose -f docker-all-services/docker-compose.yaml logs -f audio

Stop without deleting local state:

docker compose -f docker-all-services/docker-compose.yaml down

Persistent Data

The all-services stack mounts:

volumes:
  - smto-all-services-data:/data

The entrypoint prepares:

Path Purpose
/data/artifacts Runtime databases, gateway registry, settings, generated SSL
/data/outputs Generated output artifacts
/data/playwright-duckai-profile Browser profile for online AI checks
/data/models/whisper Whisper model files

Inspect volumes:

docker volume ls
docker volume inspect smto_smto-all-services-data

The exact volume name can be prefixed by the Compose project name.

Install Required Gateways

The gateway is the process that touches the real shell. It is required for command-backed agent work, terminal sessions, gateway-routed tasks, and the UI LLM launch controls. Install it natively on every machine that should execute commands.

On the Docker host:

./src/gateway_agent/install.sh
./src/gateway_agent/startup.sh

On a native Windows host, use the PowerShell gateway:

.\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1
.\src\gateway_windows\startup.ps1

Native Windows v1 supports PowerShell /exec, /exec/stream, and /exec/cancel. For POSIX terminal workflows on Windows, run the Linux gateway inside WSL and register it as a separate Linux gateway node.

Verify from the host:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/capabilities

Verify from the server container:

docker exec smto-all-server curl -s http://host.docker.internal:8787/healthz
docker exec smto-all-server curl -s http://host.docker.internal:8787/capabilities

For a gateway on another trusted machine:

GATEWAY_NODE_NAME=workstation ./src/gateway_agent/startup.sh --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8787

Add it in the Agent UI Gateway drawer with a nickname, host, port, and node. The gateway exposes /healthz, /capabilities, /exec, /exec/stream, /exec/cancel, and profile-specific optional routes such as /terminal/ws and /llm/*. It does not include built-in authentication. Keep it on loopback or a trusted network boundary.

flowchart TD UI[Agent UI] --> Runtime[Agent runtime] Runtime --> Registry[Gateway registry] Registry --> A[Gateway A\nlocalhost\nhost shell] Registry --> B[Gateway B\nworkstation\nremote shell] Registry --> C[Gateway C\nbuild-node\nserver shell] A --> TA[PTY terminal and workspace] B --> TB[PTY terminal and workspace] C --> TC[PTY terminal and workspace]

Attach An Existing LLM Endpoint

The Dockerized runtime calls an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The endpoint must provide:

  • GET /v1/models
  • POST /v1/chat/completions

Verify an existing endpoint from the host:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer local'

If the endpoint runs on the Docker host and the server container cannot reach 127.0.0.1, use host.docker.internal or the host LAN IP in the Agent UI LLM Endpoint settings:

http://host.docker.internal:8000/v1

Verify from the server container:

docker exec smto-all-server curl -s http://host.docker.internal:8000/v1/models \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer local'

Use Model = auto when /v1/models returns the model id you want. Use an explicit model id when the server requires one.

Or Host vLLM Locally With Conda

Use this path when you want the same machine to host an OpenAI-compatible vLLM server. Current vLLM quickstart guidance supports creating a Python 3.12 conda environment and installing vLLM through uv. Upstream references: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/quickstart/ and https://vllm.ai/releases.

conda create -n vllm python=3.12 -y
conda activate vllm
pip install --upgrade uv
uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto

Then launch one of the repository profiles:

./src/llm/start-current-qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-awq.sh

Smaller first-launch option:

./src/llm/start-qwen2.5-1.5b-instruct.sh

Verify:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer local'

MAX_MODEL_LEN=8192 ./src/llm/start-current-qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-awq.sh

The Agent UI Settings drawer can also start or stop the configured local LLM command through the gateway. The defaults are:

conda env: vllm
command: ./src/llm/start-current-qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-awq.sh
cwd: workspace root

Those controls call /api/agent/llm/status, /api/agent/llm/start, /api/agent/llm/stop, and /api/agent/llm/log, which proxy to the selected gateway's /llm/* routes.

Docker Runtime Configuration

Agent UI runtime controls are persisted in the backend settings database. YAML is optional legacy bootstrap only. If you need a bootstrap file, mount it and set AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH:

services:
  server:
    environment:
      AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH: /data/config.yaml
    volumes:
      - smto-all-services-data:/data
      - ../config.yaml:/data/config.yaml:ro

Example LLM bootstrap:

llm:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8000/v1
  api_key: local
  default_model: auto
  default_temperature: 0.1
  timeout_seconds: 120
  max_tokens: 0
  context_window_tokens: 32768
runtime:
  run_store_path: artifacts/runtime.db

Keep secrets out of committed config files.

Server-Only Docker Stack

Use the smaller docker/ stack only when you want the Agent runtime and manual without the website and audio service:

./docker/build.sh
./docker/start.sh

That stack uses the same Dockerfile with the default AOR_BUILD_AUDIO=0, so it does not build whisper-cli.

Or use the compatibility launcher:

./docker/start-server.sh

Open:

Page URL
Agent UI http://127.0.0.1:8011/agent-ui
Manual http://127.0.0.1:8013/manual

The same gateway and LLM requirements apply.

Enable HTTPS

For Docker:

AOR_SSL_ENABLED=1 ./docker-all-services/start.sh

The container generates or reuses a self-signed certificate under /data/artifacts/ssl/.

Open:

https://127.0.0.1:8011/agent-ui

Browsers warn because this is a local development certificate.

Health Checks

From the host:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8011/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8013/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8014/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8787/healthz
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models -H 'Authorization: Bearer local'

From inside the server container:

docker exec smto-all-server curl -s http://host.docker.internal:8787/healthz
docker exec smto-all-server curl -s http://host.docker.internal:8000/v1/models \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer local'

Then submit a read-only request:

What repository workspace can you see, and what files are at the root?

If the gateway is connected and shell execution is allowed by policy, the runtime routes read-only commands through the gateway and renders command capsules in the response.

sequenceDiagram participant User participant Compose as Docker Compose participant Server as Agent runtime participant Gateway participant LLM User->>Compose: ./docker-all-services/start.sh Compose->>Server: Start Agent UI/API User->>Gateway: Start native gateway User->>LLM: Start existing /v1 endpoint or vLLM User->>Server: curl /healthz User->>Gateway: curl /healthz User->>LLM: curl /v1/models User->>Server: Open /agent-ui and submit prompt Server->>Gateway: Validated shell command Gateway-->>Server: stdout, stderr, exit code Server->>LLM: Structured model calls Server-->>User: Final answer and evidence

Troubleshooting

If the UI does not open:

docker compose -f docker-all-services/docker-compose.yaml ps
docker compose -f docker-all-services/docker-compose.yaml logs server

If the gateway works on the host but not from Docker, check the container-side host:

docker exec smto-all-server curl -s http://host.docker.internal:8787/healthz

If a remote gateway fails, verify its bind host, firewall, node name, and the Agent UI gateway registry entry.

If model calls fail, test /v1/models from both host and container. Use host.docker.internal, a LAN IP, or a mounted bootstrap config if the endpoint is not reachable at 127.0.0.1.

If vLLM fails to load, lower context or choose a smaller profile:

MAX_MODEL_LEN=8192 ./src/llm/start-current-qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-awq.sh
./src/llm/start-qwen2.5-1.5b-instruct.sh

If Docker state looks stale, inspect /data:

docker exec -it smto-all-server bash
ls /data
ls /data/artifacts

Remove the data volume only when you intentionally want to erase local runtime state.
